texts: On day 17 of Year 1, Keepers had relit the eleven lanterns of the Middle Row.
The dim lanterns gave weak mist-light.
The weak mist-light attracted a handful of nightmoths.
Keepers counted twelve nightmoths at the Middle Row that night.
The thread harvest at the Middle Row fell.
Pell and Coraline Ash collected a handful of silken threads from the Middle Row the next morning.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water at Cauldron Hall that day.
The cauldrons yielded two vessels of mire-essence.
The cauldrons had yielded three vessels of mire-essence on day 1.

q1_issues.issue: (Member sk_lanterns_1 dim) predicates a member property on the group symbol, which the instruction set forbids ('a bare (Member <group> <prop>) appears only for a property genuinely of the collection itself'); a descriptive modifier on a definite plural must distribute via the per-member rule, exactly as the parse's own burn rule does.

(LocatedIn sk_cauldrons_1 cauldron_hall) asserts a location the text never states, inferred from the venue named in the previous sentence -- 'no unstated property, possessor, location or causal link, however obvious'.

'in sea-water' is the substance the boiling is done in, and slotting it as a second Location beside the venue 'at Cauldron Hall' gives one event two places; Instrument is the role the instruction set defines for 'a tool, substance or conduit'.

q2_gaps: A bare capitalized plural role-word ('Keepers', twice, with no determiner): the capitalized-label rule covers singular-collective 'the Assembly' and the definite plural name 'the Wrens', but not a bare capitalized plural, so neither its Name-vs-common-noun status nor whether the second mention corefers is decidable.

A past perfect whose only ordering target is in a DIFFERENT sentence of the passage: the rule says to emit Before 'whenever the sentence contains another asserted event', while the exclusion is 'a past perfect with no other event in the text' -- the two wordings disagree, and this passage has both shapes ('had relit' before the burning, 'had yielded' before the yielding).

A distributive predicate with a plural subject AND a plural object ('Keepers had relit the eleven lanterns'): the mandated per-member rule over the subject group would assert that each keeper relit all eleven lanterns, so the instruction set's distribution doctrine has no correct form here.

A measure / container 'of' phrase ('two vessels of mire-essence'): explicitly excluded from the genitive Possession mapping but given no positive encoding, so the count-of-containers vs Measure-with-'unspecified'-scale choice is undetermined.

A medium / substance PP on an event ('boiled the threads in sea-water'): Location is defined as 'in/at/on ...' while Instrument is defined as covering a 'substance', and no rule separates a medium from a venue.
review.notes: Term propagation for 'that night' / 'the next morning' / 'that day' (day+1, year carried, day-part, Before), the coordinated-subject distribution with a shared object, the scalar-change Theme on 'the harvest fell', the CardinalityPhrase for 'a handful', and the silken/mist/night compound decompositions are all handled exactly as instructed. The parse applies the past-perfect Before across sentences for 'had yielded' (statement 101) but not for 'had relit', which is internally inconsistent whichever reading of that rule is intended.

issues.reason: Categorical statements states that a descriptive modifier or copular predicate on a plural 'always goes through the distributive rule' and that a bare (Member <group> <prop>) 'appears only for a property genuinely of the collection itself', so (Member sk_lanterns_1 dim) asserts the group-as-object is dim — the reading the plural rules explicitly warn against, and inconsistent with the parse's own per-member burn rule over the same group.

Core patterns bars 'no unstated property, possessor, location or causal link, however obvious', and the text never says where the cauldrons are — the atom is inferred from the previous sentence's venue and from the words inside the name 'Cauldron Hall', which carry no content at all since a multi-word name is non-compositional (Names and casing).

Location is defined precisely as the 'in/at/on ...' oblique and the surface preposition here is 'in'; nothing in the instruction set bars two Location atoms on one event, the filler is a true and well-typed bare-mass constant with its compound genus emitted, and the reviewer's own fifth gap concedes that no rule separates a medium from a venue — an objection to graceful improvisation in gap territory.

gaps_confirmed: A bare, determinerless capitalized plural role-word ('Keepers'): the capitalized-label rule covers singular-collective 'the Assembly' and definite-plural 'the Wrens' but not this shape, leaving its Name-vs-common-noun status and cross-sentence coreference undecidable.

Past-perfect ordering whose only target sits in a different sentence: the rule says to emit Before 'whenever the sentence contains another asserted event' while the exclusion is 'no other event in the text' — the two wordings disagree, and this passage contains both shapes.

A distributive predicate with a plural subject AND a plural object ('Keepers had relit the eleven lanterns'): the mandated per-member rule over the subject group would assert that each keeper relit all eleven lanterns, so the distribution doctrine has no correct form here.

A measure / container 'of' phrase ('two vessels of mire-essence'): explicitly excluded from the genitive Possession mapping but given no positive encoding, so counting containers vs a Measure with an 'unspecified' scale is undetermined.

A medium / substance PP on an event ('boiled the threads in sea-water'): Location is defined as 'in/at/on ...' while Instrument's gloss covers 'a substance', and no rule separates a medium from a venue.
new_gaps: A first-mention definite plural whose only anchor is a named venue ('the cauldrons' right after 'at Cauldron Hall'): the bridging rule licenses a link atom only for a part-whole definite (PartOf to its antecedent) and supplies no locative counterpart, so the compliant parse must leave such a definite wholly unanchored — a licensed form would need a way to record that a bridged definite is anchored to the salient place without asserting a position the text never states.

A descriptive modifier on an ANAPHORIC definite plural ('The dim lanterns', re-mentioning a group whose dimness the previous clause already conveyed): the instruction set does not say whether a modifier on a re-mention is a fresh distributive assertion or mere re-description, and asserting it again counts as new evidence for a fact already in the parse.
adjudication.defect_summary: For the dim-lanterns atom the compliant form is the per-member distribution rule (: lanterns_dim (Implication (PartOf $x sk_lanterns_1) (Member $x dim)) (STV 1.0 0.9)) in place of (Member sk_lanterns_1 dim); for the cauldrons the compliant form emits no location atom at all — (GroupOf sk_cauldrons_1 cauldron) plus the yield event is the whole of what the text licenses, since nothing in the sentence places them.
adjudication.notes: Everything else is handled as instructed — term propagation for 'that night' / 'the next morning' / 'that day', the coordinated-subject distribution over one shared thread group, the Name-plus-type treatment of 'the Middle Row' and 'Cauldron Hall', and the compound genera (mist_light, nightmoth, silken_thread, sea_water, mire_essence). The 'had relit' / 'had yielded' asymmetry the reviewer notes falls squarely on the second confirmed gap's wording disagreement rather than on a rule the parse breaks, so I left it as a gap and not an issue.
